title: Connect All Offices at Minimum Cost
real_world_story: The organization has a list of all possible network cables it could install between offices, each with a cabling cost. It must choose a subset of these cables that connects every office while spending as little as possible overall.

real_world_connection.input_represents: All candidate cables and their installation costs
real_world_connection.output_represents: The minimum total cost to connect every office
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Building a minimum spanning network (spanning tree)

problem_statement: Given N offices numbered 0 to N-1 and E candidate undirected cables with costs, find the minimum total cost required to connect all N offices into a single connected network.
task: Return the total cost of the minimum-cost spanning network. If the graph cannot connect all offices, return -1.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain three integers u v w describing a candidate cable between offices u and v with installation cost w.
output_format: Print the minimum total installation cost that connects all offices, or -1 if they cannot all be connected.

examples.explanation: The cheapest way to connect all offices uses the cables 2-3 (4), 0-3 (5) and 0-1 (10), for a total of 19.

expected_algorithm.name: Kruskal's Algorithm
expected_algorithm.reason: Sorting candidate cables by cost and adding the cheapest cable that does not create a cycle yields the minimum-cost spanning tree.

hint: Sort all candidate cables by installation cost.
Add each candidate in order if it connects two still-unconnected groups.
Use a union-find structure to track which offices are already connected.
Stop once N - 1 cables have been selected.
real_world_takeaway: Kruskal's algorithm lets an organization build a fully connected office network at the minimum installation cost by choosing the cheapest non-redundant cables.
